title: Universal lifting property of an algebraic-space blowup
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal on the small etale site [def-sfb-space-quasi-coherent-ideal]; finite type means locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $b:B=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal K}X\to X$ be the algebraic-space blowup, meaning a blowup presentation of [def-sfb-space-blowup-presentation], or equivalently the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal K^n$ obtained by etale descent of the scheme blowups. For a morphism $f:Y\to X$, form the extended ideal $\mathcal K_Y=\operatorname{im}(f^*\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_Y)$ with tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. If $\mathcal K_Y$ is etale locally generated by a non-zero-divisor (that is, its closed subspace is an effective Cartier divisor), then there exists a unique morphism $\widetilde f:Y\to B$ over $S$ such that $b\circ\widetilde f=f$. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, reducedness, or density assumption is imposed on $X$ or $Y$.

proof.text: Put $J=\mathcal K_Y$ and $\mathcal R=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal K^n$. The ideal-power definitions and affine-chart calculus identify $\mathcal K^n$ with the image of multiplication $\mathcal K^{\otimes n}\to\mathcal O_X$; these images are quasi-coherent, and $\mathcal R$ is generated in degree one. Since $J$ is locally $(t)$ for a non-zero-divisor $t$, multiplication $J^{\otimes n}\to J^n$ is an isomorphism: locally it sends the basis $t^{\otimes n}$ to the basis $t^n$ (also for $n=0$). These local identifications agree on overlaps because both are multiplication. In particular $J$ is a line module.

The canonical tensor-pullback map $f^*\mathcal K\twoheadrightarrow J$ extends degreewise to $\psi_n:f^*(\mathcal K^n)\to J^n\simeq J^{\otimes n}$. Indeed the canonical map to $\mathcal O_Y$ sends a product of $n$ local sections of $\mathcal K$ to the product of their images in $J$, so its image lies in $J^n$; all sections of $\mathcal K^n$ are locally sums of such products. Factoring through this submodule is unique. Associativity and the unit law hold after inclusion in $\mathcal O_Y$, hence hold before inclusion. Thus the $\psi_n$ form a graded unital algebra map $\psi:f^*\mathcal R\to\bigoplus J^{\otimes n}$, and $\psi_1$ is surjective by the definition of $J$ as the sheaf image. This uses no injectivity of $f^*\mathcal K\to\mathcal O_Y$.

Apply the degree-one line-quotient lemma to $(f,J,\psi)$: the preceding steps verify its quasi-coherence, degree-one generation, line-module and surjectivity hypotheses. It gives $r:Y\to P_X(\mathcal R)$ over $X$. Identify $P_X(\mathcal R)$ with the given $B$ by its blowup presentation, namely the same Rees Proj on every affine etale chart. Its composite $\widetilde f:Y\to B$ satisfies $b\widetilde f=f$.

For uniqueness let $h_1,h_2:Y\to B$ be over $X$, and put $D=V(J)$ and $U=Y\setminus D$. The blowup-chart theorem makes $b$ proper and an isomorphism over $X\setminus V(\mathcal K)$, so $h_1|_U=h_2|_U$. Properness includes separatedness; its diagonal is representable by closed immersions. Consequently the equalizer $E=Y\times_{(h_1,h_2),B\times_XB,\Delta_b}B\hookrightarrow Y$ is a closed subspace containing $U$. On an affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ where $J=(t)$ with $t$ a non-zero-divisor, its defining ideal $H\subseteq A$ restricts to zero on $D(t)$. For $a\in H$, vanishing in $A_t$ means $t^na=0$ for some $n$, hence $a=0$. Thus $H=0$ on every such chart, and $E=Y$. The fibre-product equalizer condition gives $h_1=h_2$. This is the explicit local proof of the density/equality argument in Tags 083S and 084N, requiring no density assumption in the statement.

Step 3: the new 085D node, plus the def-sfb-space-blowup-presentation identification P_X(R)≅B. That identification is genuine: V-automorphisms of Bl_{I_V}V are trivial (separated, and an isomorphism over the dense complement of the center per lem-sfb-space-blowup-chart-properties), so the chart identifications glue with no twisted forms. Step 4: b proper and an isomorphism off V(K) (chart-properties, finite-type K), so the diagonal is a closed immersion and the equalizer is a closed subspace E containing U. On an affine chart with J=(t), A→A_t is injective, so H=0, E=Y and h1=h2. This writes out 083S/084N, so no node is needed (C1 exception).
